newsitem.title: GERMANY: DHL sees global logistic centre expansion.
newsitem.headline: DHL sees global logistic centre expansion.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said on Friday it planned to open a network of international logistics centres around the globe to expand the courier company's services.

DHL business logistics manager, Norbert Milzarek, said the integrator saw warehousing and distribution as a way to retain clients with new services while maintaining transportation as the company's core business.
"Previously we said we did not do outsourcing of warehousing. Now, we say yes, we will offer it to clients," he said at the Transport '97 trade fair in Munich.
Global clients looking for a one-stop complete range of services could use the DHL logistics network to operate a worldwide 24-hour customer service.
Up to 25 percent of total company costs were often logistics and transport costs with firms increasingly seeking to outsource logistics services due to cost saving pressures, Milzarek noted.

The existing eight DHL-run Express Logistics Centres (ELC) in Brussels, Miami, Panama, Bahrain, Johannnesburg, Hong Kong, Singapore and Brisbane, offering storage, 24-hour delivery to surrounding markets and added services such as part-assembly or repairs for different clients, would be expanded over the next few years.
" There will be one ELC in central Europe, perhaps two in North America, perhaps one in Latin America over the next 2-3 years and a maximum of 15 worldwide," he forecast.

DHL was currently seeking experienced warehouse operators, including one partner in each EU country, to run Distribution Centres (DC) providing complete outsourced warehousing and distribution services for individual customers with large volumes.
The first DC opened in Amsterdam last year as the European distribution hub of VLSI Technology and other centres could be opened according to client demand, Miliarek said.
Strategic Parts Centres (SPC) for small numbers of key parts would be opened in city locations for rapid, on-site repair services or electronic maintenance systems, he added.
Locations for seven or eight European centres would be decided within the coming few weeks with a total of 35 locations planned for Europe and 15 more around the globe.
Four SPCs already exist in Germany in Frankfurt, Munich, Leipzig and Hamburg and three others in other European locations. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
